newsitem.title: USA: Texaco to sell chemical unit for $600 million.
newsitem.headline: Texaco to sell chemical unit for $600 million.

text.p: Texaco Inc. said Tuesday it would sell a gasoline additive business to Huntsman Corp. for about $600 million, the last of a string of sales of chemical businesses.

The unit being sold makes ethers used to help reduce auto exhaust pollutants and is located next to Huntsman facilities at Port Neches, Tex., Texaco said. Huntsman has operated the plant for Texaco since operations began there in August 1994.
Huntsman said the acquisition would make it the second largest producer of methyl tertiary butyl ether (mtbe).

MTBE is added to gasoline to help reduce carbon monoxide emissions, making it burn more cleanly, as well as to increase octane. MTBE has been used to reduce smog and attain mandated air quality standards in certain regions of the United States under the Clean Air Act of 1990.
"This is the last major step in the sale of Texaco's chemical business and is in keeping with our plans to focus on our core oil and gas business," Texaco Chairman Peter Bijur said in a statement.
He said Huntsman would continue to be both a customer of and supplier to Texaco.
As part of the agreement, Huntsman said it would also acquire Texaco's MTBE manufacturing technology, and the right to license that technology around the world.
"This acquisition will greatly enhance our product integration and diversification," Huntsman Chairman Jon Huntsman said.
Huntsman said it and Texaco had also negotiated a long-term MTBE supply agreement.
Huntsman also said it entered a long-term agreement with BASF AG and BASF would receive a significant portion of the Port Neches propylene oxide production.
Propylene oxide is a petrochemical used in home furnishings, construction, packaging, transportation and other industries.
The company said it had worked closely with Texaco for three years to acquire the business, and it was the second largest financial transaction in the company's history.
The deal was expected to close in the first quarter 1997, Huntsman said.
